column5: Our Downloads window has three icon buttons, all named Remove, one per active transfer. Files can have the same filename but different folders. Voice Control users report guessing which one to say. How would you change the naming without renaming the underlying files or disabling ordinary clicks?
column6: Preserve the visible action term and distinguish targets using stable user-facing context, including duplicate filenames; accept contextual labels or suitable alternative names, not opaque identifiers.

column5: The sidebar hosts an AppKit search field in SwiftUI. Both the wrapper and the editable field announce Search and people encounter two stops. The AppKit field handles selection and insertion. What would you change, and what should stay editable?
column6: Expose one editable owner rather than replacing it with a static wrapper; accept native forwarding or leaving the wrapper non-actionable. Preserve editing, current value and ordinary input.

column5: Two document windows can each open their own inspector. Closing the inspector in one window sometimes sends keyboard input to the other document. How would you structure ownership of the return destination?
column6: Bind restoration to the particular window and presentation; verify current membership and eligibility, not just global most recent field.

column5: Our inspector overlays text on a blurred album cover. With Reduce Transparency on, the cover is still visible behind the text. Show how you would choose a background while keeping selection, keyboard focus and editing in the same inspector.
column6: Use an opaque readable fallback for the relevant environment without recreating controls or altering focus; do not claim a color token alone establishes contrast against artwork.

column5: A folder row can stay selected while the user expands and collapses it. Our outline describes every selected folder as expanded even if its children are hidden. What state should the row and disclosure action expose?
column6: Separate expansion from selection; update expansion on disclosure and retain independently actionable children and stable selection.

column5: A background export finishes while I am typing in a rename field. We want people to know about the export, but keystrokes must keep going into the field. How would you signal this without redirecting input?
column6: Use a scoped status or announcement on the meaningful transition; do not move first responder or repeatedly announce unchanged status.

column5: Our button visibly says Continue, but its accessible name is Step 3 of 4. Voice Control users try saying the displayed word. We still need to communicate progress. How should these pieces be represented?
column6: Keep the action identifiable using its visible name; expose progress as context or value rather than substituting it for the action.

column5: Each row says Play, button, double tap to activate. One row streams over mobile data when activated. Which information belongs in its name or hint, and what should be left to the system?
column6: Keep meaningful name and role; avoid repeating generic gestures and distinguish non-obvious consequences. Accept no hint on ordinary rows.

column5: A download screen receives 30 updates per second. People want to inspect the current percentage whenever they visit, but speech keeps interrupting the rest of the screen. What would you expose and when would you notify?
column6: Keep the current value available on demand; separate continuous value updates from bounded meaningful transition notifications, including completion.

column5: Our custom scrubber has discrete chapters of different lengths, plus a plain tap to play. Dragging works but people using an adjustable action can land between chapters. How should adjustment behave at either end?
column6: Operate in discrete chapter space with directional bounds; preserve ordinary play and state/value updates. Accept native controls or equivalent semantic representation.

column5: The legal viewer ships with a shortcut for jumping between warnings. First-time VoiceOver users who haven't learned the rotor still need to find the warnings, and some chapters have none. How should the page behave?
column6: Keep warnings in ordinary reading/navigation, supplement with shortcut, handle no matches without removing content. Do not force rotor familiarity.

column5: Two text fields can both fail validation with the same message. When the form updates, a user cannot tell which field the error belongs to. How would you fix this while preserving the text and editing position?
column6: Associate each error with the correct field and preserve input and identity; do not merge two editable controls or announce every keystroke.

column5: A horizontal shelf has a sponsored tile at the end. Moving Right from it keeps bouncing to the first tile, and moving Down never reaches the next shelf. How would you review this focus behavior while preserving Select on every tile?
column6: Examine directional destinations and intervening guides or overrides, preserve an exit and ordinary select; do not treat array order alone as directional navigation proof.

column5: The details screen should start on Resume. If I move to Extras while artwork is loading, focus jumps back to Resume when the image arrives. When should the initial target be chosen?
column6: Apply initial focus for a new presentation once; incidental content refresh must not reassert it over a valid user choice.

column5: While someone is browsing live channels, a filter removes the focused channel. The list can become empty. How should the next focus target be chosen without opening a channel?
column6: Resolve a surviving eligible target or persistent empty-state/filter control; separate focus from activation. Do not request a removed item.

column5: Product wants titles readable from a couch. A long German title in our tvOS SwiftUI detail header crowds out Play and Details. What would you change on a 26.0 deployment target, and what would you condition on a newer SDK?
column6: Preserve both actions and readable content via flexible layout; distinguish supported behavior on the deployment target from later tvOS facilities; avoid importing iOS availability assumptions.

column5: A language tile under the remote cursor announces Selected before I press Select. Moving away also clears the actual selected language. How should highlighting and committed choice interact?
column6: Keep transient focus/highlight distinct from committed selection; activation changes the choice. Preserve accurate accessible state on old and new tiles.

column5: On our sports shelf a red border means Live, but focus also adds a border. Some viewers cannot tell which event is live. How would you communicate both facts without changing what Select does?
column6: Add a non-color live cue and accessible state independent of focus styling, retain ordinary activation and update the cue when the event ends.
